title: Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Light, fluffy pancakes with crisp edges. A weekend staple.

steps.heading: Mix the dry
steps.body: In a {tool:bowl-large}, whisk together {ingredient:flour}, {ingredient:sugar}, {ingredient:baking-powder}, {ingredient:baking-soda}, and {ingredient:salt} until evenly combined.

notes.body: Whisking the dry ingredients is the easiest way to skip sifting.

steps.heading: Mix the wet
steps.body: In a {tool:bowl-medium}, whisk {ingredient:buttermilk}, {ingredient:eggs}, and {ingredient:vanilla} until uniform. Stream in the melted {ingredient:butter} while whisking so it does not seize.

notes.body: Adding warm butter slowly into the cold buttermilk keeps it emulsified instead of forming butter beads.

steps.heading: Combine and rest
steps.body: Pour the wet into the dry. Fold with a {tool:spatula} **just until** the flour disappears — lumps are fine. Let the batter rest.

notes.body: Do not overmix. Overworked gluten makes pancakes tough.
Resting lets the flour hydrate; pancakes puff more reliably.

steps.heading: Heat the pan
steps.body: Set the {tool:skillet} over medium heat. Brush with a thin film of {ingredient:butter}. Drop a few water beads on — they should sizzle and skate, not evaporate instantly.

notes.body: Test temperature with water before sacrificing a pancake. If beads vanish, the pan is too hot.

steps.heading: Cook the pancakes
steps.body: Ladle ~⅓ cup batter per pancake into the {tool:skillet}. Cook until bubbles form across the surface and the edges look set, about 2 minutes.

notes.body: Drop blueberries or chocolate chips onto the wet side now, before flipping.

steps.heading: Flip and finish
steps.body: Flip with the {tool:spatula} and cook until the second side is golden and the center springs back, ~1 minute. Move to a plate and repeat with the remaining batter.

notes.body: Hold finished pancakes in a 200°F / 95°C oven on a rack so they stay crisp.
No buttermilk? Stir 1½ tsp lemon juice into 1½ cups whole milk and let sit 5 minutes.
